codes.justification: The clause addresses disagreement over toxic or hazardous substances at the Place of the Work, requiring an independent expert investigation into their existence and origin.
The clause allocates responsibility for resolving disputes over hazardous substance origin and funds an independent expert to determine liability, reflecting risk allocation and management.
Requires joint preparation of a schedule for ordering cash allowance items to avoid delaying the progress of the Work, directly addressing sequencing/timing of Work activities.
The schedule is specifically intended to ensure timely ordering of allowance items to avoid delays arising from procurement/delivery of Products required for the Work.
Requires the Trade Contractor and Construction Manager to jointly plan procurement timing, reflecting collaborative planning between parties.
The clause requires parties to attempt amicable negotiation and disclosure of facts as part of the dispute resolution process outlined in PART 8, directly establishing a dispute resolution procedure.

The clause establishes a general duty on the Contractor to provide and pay for labour, Products, equipment, and services necessary for performance of the Work in accordance with the Contract, which is a broad execution obligation.
The clause establishes a mediation procedure involving the Project Mediator to resolve unresolved disputes following the negotiation process, in accordance with CCDC 40 mediation rules.
The clause governs the Consultant's review and certification process for the Contractor's application for final payment, a core payment procedure under the Contract.

The clause obligates the Trade Contractor to correct or pay for damage resulting from corrections made under the warranty correction provisions, directly addressing consequences and remediation of defective work.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Trade Contractor for damage arising from correction work, assigning risk/liability for such consequential damage.
The clause allocates responsibility for patent infringement claims and related costs to the Contractor, including an indemnity/hold harmless obligation, which is a form of risk allocation.

The clause preserves the Trade Contractor's obligations for quality, correction, and warranty of work performed prior to termination, directly addressing correction of non-conforming or defective work.
The clause allocates continuing responsibility to the Trade Contractor for conformity of work performed even after contract termination, an allocation of contractual risk/responsibility.

The clause addresses toxic and hazardous substances at the Place of the Work, expressly assigning deemed control and management to the Owner for existing conditions under applicable environmental/hazardous substance legislation.
The clause allocates legal responsibility (deemed control and management) for pre-existing hazardous conditions to the Owner, a risk allocation provision.

The clause establishes that the Contract represents a fixed baseline agreement that may only be amended through mechanisms provided in the Contract Documents, reflecting a lock-in of the agreed terms subject to formal change processes.
The clause restricts amendments to the Contract to those made through the Contract Documents' formal change provisions, directly relating to how changes to the agreement must be processed.
The clause governs the process for proposing changes in the Work and adjusting the Fee for Construction Services and Contract Time, a core Change Order mechanism.
Clause cross-references provisions governing toxic and hazardous substances and mould, which are environmental concerns arising from concealed conditions.
Clause allocates responsibility for handling concealed or unknown conditions by directing parties to specific governing provisions, reflecting risk allocation for these situations.

This clause is part of the Changes in the Work part, addressing discovery of concealed or unknown site conditions that may trigger a change; requires notice before disturbing conditions to preserve rights to claims/adjustments.
The clause allocates responsibility for identifying and notifying concealed/unknown site conditions that differ materially from those anticipated, managing risk between the parties.
The clause assigns the Contractor responsibility for construction means, methods, techniques, and procedures, establishing a core Work-execution duty.
The clause explicitly includes responsibility for sequences and coordinating the various parts of the Work, addressing sequencing of the Work.
The clause grants the Construction Manager and Consultant authority to reject non-conforming work and to require inspection or testing of work whether fabricated, installed or completed.
The authority to reject work that does not conform to the Contract Documents addresses identification and rejection of non-conforming work.
The clause references preparation of Change Orders and Change Directives under the relevant change provisions.

Clause is part of Part 8 Dispute Resolution and addresses retention of rights/recourses contingent on Notice in Writing under the dispute resolution provisions, forming part of the dispute process framework.
The clause establishes the timing/dating requirements for progress payment applications, which is part of the payment application and certification mechanics under the Contract.
Clause governs the Owner's ability to object to and control selection of Subcontractors/Suppliers who will perform portions of the Work, a matter of organizing execution of the Work.

The clause allocates responsibility between the Owner and Construction Manager for obtaining and paying for approvals, permits, and easements, establishing a clear risk/responsibility allocation for regulatory compliance obligations.
The clause requires adjustments to Contract Price and Time resulting from delays to be processed through Change Order and Change Directive mechanisms.

The clause provides for adjustments in cost or time through Change Order or Change Directive procedures when discoveries impact the Work, directly invoking the formal change mechanisms under GC 6.2 and GC 6.3.
The clause governs monthly applications for payment on account, including payment of Reimbursable Costs, and references Payment Legislation and payment article, directly addressing payment mechanics.
Payments may be tied to progress of Design Services and Work or achievement of a milestone, linking payment timing to the Milestone Schedule.

This clause establishes broad duties for the Design/Construction Team to perform the Work, procure subconsultants/subcontractors, arrange testing and commissioning, and complete tasks required for Ready-for-Takeover during the Construction Phase.
The clause requires completion of remaining Design Services under PMT oversight, reflecting coordination between design and construction activities.
The clause requires the Contractor to submit a schedule of values to facilitate evaluation of applications for payment, directly governing the payment application process.

The clause defines when a suspension is deemed to have occurred, allocating consequences/responsibility for work stoppages not caused by the Contractor, which is a risk allocation mechanism under the default/termination provisions.
The clause addresses consistency between Construction Documents and the requirements of the Contract Documents, requiring disclosure of deviations for review.
Accepted deviations from the Owner's Statement of Requirements are formally recorded via a Change Order, invoking the change mechanism of the Contract.
The clause requires a schedule for ordering allowance items specifically to avoid delaying progress of the Work, linking procurement/ordering timing to schedule impact.
The clause requires joint preparation of a schedule addressing timing of ordering items, an element of sequencing the Work.
The clause provides for extension of Contract Time and adjustment of Contractor's Fee, GMP, and Target Contract Price as a result of delay events, effectively adjusting contract terms.
The clause explicitly states that the Contractor's Fee, the GMP and the Target Contract Price shall be adjusted as a result of the delay, directly administering the GMP/Target Cost mechanism.
The clause allocates risk for delays caused by events beyond the Contractor's control (labour disputes, weather, subcontractor default) by granting time and cost relief, reflecting risk allocation.
Reference to 'unusual delay by common carriers' ties schedule impact to delivery/transport of goods required for the Work.
The clause requires Shop Drawings to be submitted to authorities having jurisdiction for approval, involving review/approval by an authorized party similar to inspection processes.
The clause addresses coordination of Shop Drawings with regulatory approval requirements to ensure compliance with applicable authority standards.
The clause establishes the Construction Manager's responsibility for proper performance of the Work in accordance with the design and Contract Documents, a broad work-execution obligation.
The clause conditions warranty responsibility on the extent the design/documents permit proper performance, which relates to responsibility for non-conforming work under warranty provisions.
The clause provides for adjustment of the Contract Time due to delay events, part of the Changes in the Work part governing time extensions and entitlement to costs.
The clause allocates risk of delay events (labour disputes, fire, weather, causes beyond control) between the parties, determining who bears schedule and cost consequences.

The clause defines the scope of the Consultant's review of Shop Drawings as limited to conformity with the design concept and general arrangement, addressing design coordination and compatibility responsibility.
The clause describes the nature and limits of the Consultant's review of Shop Drawings, which functions as a review/inspection mechanism prior to incorporation into the Work.
The clause establishes that the Contract Price includes a contingency allowance as stated in the Owner's Statement of Requirements, relating to the pricing/cost structure of the Contract.

The clause establishes procedures requiring the Construction Manager to notify the Consultant and arrange inspections by authorities having jurisdiction, directly addressing inspection duties and notification requirements.

The clause establishes the Consultant's duty to conduct reviews/inspections of the Work to verify completion status for Ready for Acceptance With Reservation and Without Reservation, which is an inspection function.
Describes the recording of agreed adjustments to Contract Price and Time in a Change Order, a core change mechanism under the Contract.
Specifies that the value of Change Order work shall be included in applications for progress payment, directly addressing payment mechanics.

This clause establishes the Trade Contractor's fundamental obligation to perform the Work required by the Contract Documents, identifying the Project, place, Construction Manager, Consultant, and Payment Certifier roles.

The clause addresses errors, omissions or inconsistencies in the Contract Documents and requires reporting to the Consultant, directly implicating consistency and coordination of the design/construction documents.

The clause allocates responsibility away from the Construction Manager for errors/omissions in the Contract Documents while requiring a reporting procedure, reflecting risk allocation regarding document conformity.

This clause establishes the general scope and intent of the Contract Documents regarding labour, Products, and services required for performance of the Work by the Trade Contractor, a foundational duty governing execution.

The clause requires the Owner to pay the Construction Manager within 28 days of invoice submission for Services properly performed up to the termination date, addressing payment timing and certification upon termination.
Clause establishes interest obligations for late payments under the Contract's payment provisions, directly governing payment mechanics.
Paragraph .2 ties interest accrual to amounts resolved through dispute resolution processes under Part 7, referencing the dispute resolution mechanism.
The clause directly governs the Contractor's obligation to proceed with a change in the Work upon receipt of a Change Directive, which is a core mechanism for adjusting the Work under the Contract.
The clause imposes a duty on the Contractor to promptly perform the changed Work, addressing how the Work is to be executed once directed.

The clause governs conditions under which the Owner may occupy part or all of the Work prior to Ready-for-Takeover, affecting how the Work's completion status and possession are managed under the Contract Documents.

The clause establishes duties for the Construction Manager to confirm the takeover date and coordinate with Trade Contractors on completing the Project, governing how the work process proceeds after Ready-for-Takeover.
The clause requires establishing a reasonable date for finishing the Project in consultation with Trade Contractors, addressing scheduling/timing of remaining work.
The clause allocates indemnification obligations between Owner and Contractor for claims arising from negligence or contractual non-performance, establishing risk allocation and its limits/waiver.

The clause imposes a duty on the Contractor to take precautions during the performance of the Work to prevent removal or damage to discovered artifacts/fossils and to notify the Consultant, which is an execution obligation governing how work is carried out around such discoveries.

The clause expressly addresses resolution of disputes and matters in question between the Contractor and Other Contractors, referencing Part 8 Dispute Resolution and arbitration consent, establishing a formal dispute process.

The clause imposes a broad duty on the Contractor to establish, initiate, maintain, and supervise health and safety precautions and programs in performing the Work, establishing a general execution obligation under the Contract Documents and applicable legislation.
The clause explicitly ties adjustment of Contract Price and Contract Time from making good damage to the change provisions (GC 6.1, 6.2, 6.3), invoking Change Order/Change Directive mechanisms.
The clause allocates responsibility for making good damage not caused by the Contractor, addressing risk allocation between parties for repair of Work/property.
The clause requires the Contractor to correct/make good damaged Work, a form of remedial work similar to correction obligations.
This clause is part of GC 6.6 governing claims for a change in Contract Price and establishes the timeframe and process by which the Consultant issues findings on such claims.
The clause requires the Trade Contractor to proceed with the Work upon receipt of a Change Directive, directly governing the mechanism for implementing changes to the Work under the Contract.
The clause imposes a duty to promptly execute the changed Work, establishing a performance obligation regarding how the Work is to be carried out following the directive.

The clause requires the Consultant to review and act on Shop Drawings, samples and other submittals, which is a quality assurance/compliance review function prior to incorporation of Products into the Work.
Review of Shop Drawings and submittals for consistency with the Construction Documents involves coordination between design and construction documentation.

The clause governs procedures for claims arising from continuing events, requiring interim and final accounting of claim amounts and grounds, consistent with claims-adjustment processes under the changes/claims regime.

The clause allocates responsibility to the Trade Contractor for proper performance of the Work, limited by the extent the design and Contract Documents permit, establishing an allocation of responsibility/risk.
The clause addresses the Trade Contractor's obligation for proper performance of the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents, a core work execution duty.
This clause establishes that amendments to the Contract must follow the formal change provisions set out in the Contract Documents, reflecting the general mechanism for adjusting the Contract.

By restricting amendments to only those provided in the Contract Documents, the clause reflects the lock-in principle that changes must follow formal contract procedures rather than informal modification.
The clause requires the Owner to demonstrate financial arrangements to fulfill payment obligations under the Contract, directly relating to the payment provisions of the Contract.

The clause governs how early occupancy by the Owner affects the performance and completion of the Work, requiring Trade Contractor agreement where early occupancy directly affects the Work's execution.
The clause allocates responsibility by requiring the Trade Contractor's agreement before early occupancy where it is directly affected, managing the risk of early occupancy impacting completion.
The clause addresses responsibility for toxic and hazardous substances at the Place of the Work, an environmental hazard, and the Owner's obligations arising from their presence.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Owner for hazardous substances not brought by the Design-Builder, including costs, delay extension, and indemnification, representing risk allocation.
The clause establishes a requirement governing the quality and standard of Products used in performing the Work, imposing an obligation as to how the Work is executed with respect to materials.
The clause governs the PMT's approval of payment applications within a specified timeframe, subject to Payment Legislation, which is a core payment administration and certification provision.

The clause requires the Owner to notify the Contractor of observed defects and deficiencies during the warranty period, directly relating to identification of non-conforming Work as a precursor to correction.

The clause establishes that the Contract, once formed, may only be amended through the mechanisms provided in the Contract Documents, reflecting a baseline that can only be modified via formal contractual provisions.

The clause establishes a duty on the Contractor to take precautions and notify the Consultant during performance of the Work regarding discoveries, which is a work execution obligation.

The clause establishes the role of the Payment Certifier to review payment applications and certify the value of Design Services, Work performed, and Products delivered, directly addressing payment certification mechanics.

The clause requires monthly applications for payment on account of the Fee for Construction Services and Cost of the Work, submitted to the Owner and Consultant, addressing the timing and submission mechanics of payment applications.
Grants the Consultant authority to reject work that does not conform to the requirements of the Contract Documents, addressing non-conforming Work.

The clause governs release of holdback payment to the Design-Builder upon certification by the Payment Certifier for Quebec subcontractor/supplier work, including timing and retention for legal hypothecs.
Clause addresses the Consultant's determination on whether concealed/unknown conditions justify an adjustment in Contract Price or Contract Time, part of the change process under Part 6.

The clause allocates responsibility to the Contractor for mould caused by its operations, requiring remediation, making good damage, reimbursement, and indemnification, effectively assigning risk and consequences of non-conforming conditions to the Contractor.
The clause addresses mould contamination and remediation, an environmental/hazardous condition affecting the Work and property.
The clause requires the Contractor to remediate mould and make good damage to the Work resulting from its own operations, akin to correcting a non-conforming condition at its own expense.

The clause establishes the Owner's right to make changes to the Work and Contract Time through Change Orders or Change Directives, which is the core mechanism for adjusting the Work under the Contract.

This clause requires the Consultant to provide written interpretations and findings on matters in question between the parties within a reasonable time, forming part of the dispute/matters-in-question resolution process under the Consultant's role.
The clause directly addresses payment under property and boiler and machinery insurance policies in the event of loss or damage, referencing the insurance provisions of GC 11.1.
The clause governs how insurance proceeds are paid to the Design-Builder, an application of payment provisions related to loss or damage events.

This clause sets out the formal notice requirements for preserving a claim or right of action that would otherwise be waived, establishing a procedural mechanism for asserting matters in question between the parties.

The clause conditions the Contractor's right to terminate on the Owner's failure to provide evidence of financing, failure of the Consultant to issue payment certificates, or failure to pay certified/awarded amounts, all tied to the Contract's payment provisions.

This clause addresses continuity of the Consultant role responsible for design services and ensures coordination of design responsibility continues without interruption after termination of the prior Consultant's engagement.
The clause governs the procedure for submitting a claim notice and supporting details under the Waiver of Claims provisions, part of the formal claims/dispute notice process between the parties.
The clause establishes the Contractor's obligation to control, direct, and supervise the Work to ensure conformity with the Contract Documents, a core Work Execution duty.

The clause allocates responsibility by defining conditions constituting Owner default, allowing the Construction Manager to formally notify default, which is a risk allocation mechanism protecting the Construction Manager.
The clause requires the Owner to actively participate in developing and documenting Project Objectives alongside the IPD Team, reflecting early collaborative involvement in project planning.
The Owner must provide geotechnical and environmental impact reports relevant to the Work, expressly invoking environmental considerations.

The clause restricts amendment of the Contract to only those methods provided in the Contract Documents, reflecting the concept of a locked-in baseline that can only be altered through formal contractual mechanisms.

The clause governs completion prerequisites and their effect on attaining Ready-for-Takeover status, a milestone in the performance of the Work, allowing deferral without delaying that status.

The clause allocates responsibility upon termination, including the Owner taking possession, assuming obligations, and compensating the Construction Manager, reflecting risk and responsibility allocation upon default.
The clause specifies payment obligations to the Construction Manager for Cost of the Work and Fee upon termination, tied to Consultant certification and Part 5 payment provisions.
The Owner is entitled to take possession of the Work and Products at the Place of the Work upon termination, addressing transfer of possession/control.

The clause requires the Contractor to furnish certificates and inspection reports relating to the Work, directly addressing inspection procedures and documentation under GC 2.3 Review and Inspection of the Work.
Clause addresses procedural timing for requiring immediate arbitration under the negotiation, mediation and arbitration process, forming part of the contract's dispute resolution mechanism.
The clause allocates responsibilities between Trade Contractor and Owner for identifying, reporting, and managing the risk of mould presence, including retaining an expert to resolve disagreement.
Mould is an environmental/hazardous condition at the Place of the Project, and the clause addresses obligations to investigate and mitigate its presence to protect persons and property.

The clause governs the Owner's obligation to make payment on account within a specified timeframe after receipt of an application for payment, and requires compliance with Payment Legislation, directly addressing payment timing and legislative compliance.

The clause requires the Owner and Trade Contractors to obtain, maintain and pay for specific insurance coverages (Automobile Liability, Aircraft/Watercraft Liability, Contractors' Equipment, Contractors' Pollution Liability) per CCDC 41 requirements, directly addressing insurance obligations under the Contract.

The clause addresses mould contamination, its remediation and disposal, which is an environmental/hazardous condition issue governed by the Contract Documents.
The clause allocates responsibility and cost consequences between Owner and Contractor depending on causation of the mould condition, reflecting risk allocation and management.

The clause addresses payment of portions of the Profit Pool at determined milestones, which is a payment mechanism under the Contract.

The clause addresses extended warranty obligations related to defects beyond the standard one-year warranty, allocating responsibility for correction/warranty performance to the warrantor rather than the Construction Manager.

Requires Subcontractors and Suppliers to promptly correct defects or deficiencies in the work during warranty periods and pay for resulting damage, directly addressing correction of non-conforming Work.
Allocates responsibility for defect correction costs and warranty enforcement between Contractor, Subcontractors and Suppliers.

The clause requires parties to engage a Project Mediator for mediated negotiations on unresolved disputes, following CCDC 40 mediation rules, directly establishing a formal dispute resolution procedure.

The clause ties expenditures under the contingency allowance to authorization and valuation through the Change Order and Change Directive provisions, directly invoking the contract's change mechanisms.

The clause allocates a specific cost obligation (payment for samples) to the Construction Manager.

References the method of adjusting Contractor's Fee as set in the Agreement, relevant to the cost-plus/fee structure administration in connection with changes.

The clause establishes the process and timelines for appointing a Project Mediator under CCDC 40 rules for mediation and arbitration, forming part of the formal dispute-resolution mechanism.
